recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Body: The Sonic Slider is the flagship tool behind Biofield Tuning itself, a weighted tuning fork hand-tuned to 93.96 Hz, the twelfth harmonic of the Schumann Resonance, Earth's own natural electromagnetic pulse. Its extended handle lets you glide it smoothly across the face, neck, and body, and practitioners and users regularly report support for relaxation, circulation, and nervous system regulation. It's the same fork Chance uses in his own sessions, and a great entry point if you want to bring this work into your own daily routine.
recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Name: The Sonic Slider

His supplements are formulated with a focus on bioavailability, so the body can actually absorb and use what you're taking rather than letting it pass through unused. It's a simple, no-nonsense approach to filling the nutritional gaps most modern diets leave behind.

recBE7KwrPCyVVZMU.Bio: Gabriel, known on air as Slick Dissident, co-hosts InnerVerse's Vibe Rant show and is a longtime recurring guest on the podcast. He teaches occult symbolism and tarot on his YouTube channel, ranging across the Major Arcana, the esoteric Enneagram, mythology and archetype, mystic linguistics, and the symbolism hidden in popular film. He is best known for Tarot-tories, his own system mapping the 22 Major Arcana and zodiac archetypes onto the geography of the United States.

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "From Pulpit to Pyramids", "body": "Isaac Layzell describes growing up in a Pentecostal household where both grandparents pastored their own churches and prayer meetings brimmed with reported healings. Sanding tables eight hours a day in his father's shop, he filled his ears with conspiracy podcasts like Stuff They Don't Want You to Know, and later spent four hours a day on The Alex Jones Show, absorbing what he now calls fear-mongering until he tuned out. Ryan Bledsoe's podcast introduced him to orgone and pyramid energy, and a search for alternative healing led him to InnerVerse, biofield tuning and the orgonite he now makes in Oregon."}, {"title": "The Craft of Orgonite", "body": "Isaac walks through his method in detail. He says real orgonite must be packed with metal from tip to base, because in his view the metal acts as an antenna and plain epoxy left on its own becomes a negative energy battery. Every piece carries a quartz crystal at least an inch long, which he believes the curing epoxy squeezes into a piezoelectric charge. He pours each pyramid in one mass rather than layers, picks colors and stones such as lapis to target chakras, and credits Don Croft, working alongside his wife Carol, with inventing modern orgonite in the late 1990s."}, {"title": "Reich's Long Shadow", "body": "Fielding a listener question, Isaac traces orgonite back to Wilhelm Reich, whose orgone accumulators alternated layers of organic and inorganic material. Chance and Isaac recount how the FDA barred Reich's devices from interstate commerce, how he landed in prison for contempt of court and how he died there shortly before his release. Isaac compares Reich's work on body armor to biofield tuning, while Chance observes that a man who fled tyranny from country to country may never have undone that conditioning, a reminder that no amount of insight makes anyone immune."}, {"title": "Sacred Shapes and Hidden Numbers", "body": "Gabe points out that cone spelled backwards is Enoch and that Prometheus carried stolen fire in a fennel stalk, a natural funnel. Isaac links Enoch to the archangel Metatron, the merkaba and the Rodin coils he sets inside his pyramids, which he says draw on vortex mathematics. Chance adds that Metatron spelled in Hebrew sums to 314, a nod to pi. Later Gabe ties Plato to Urania, the muse he links to geometry, and Isaac floats his theory that the Earth is neither a globe nor flat but a donut-shaped torus."}, {"title": "Knowing Your Worth", "body": "Chance urges Isaac to raise his prices, arguing that undervaluing art and healing tools weakens them in the buyer's mind and that a price should reflect the coherence a maker cultivates across a whole life. Isaac agrees he needs to value himself more, admitting sales slowed after a strong first month. Gabe adds a lesson on classical magnanimity, warning that giving away all your apples leaves you impoverished. Isaac offers listeners the code InnerVerse for 10 percent off and closes by urging everyone to love and forgive, while Gabe praises him as proof that the next generation is arriving."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Isaac Layzell is the creative mind behind Oregon-ite, which is the website where he provides his Orgonite wares. Known for being a good-vibes generator, orgonite has potentially vast applications, from EMF mitigation to enhancing the qualities of water. Tonight we'll learn about Isaac's journey to creativity and his orgonite mission.
